text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said on Thursday it believes that it found evidence of misconduct by short sellers of its stock.

"The implications of the documents could be far reaching and, in addition to the short-sellers, involve certain members of the media and our basic trust in fairness of the American business system," Solv-Ex chairman and chief executive John Renadall said in a statement.

Solv-Ex said that in its view, the short-sellers appear to have engaged in serious wrongdoing and their conduct could provide a basis for further civil actions against other individuals by Solv-Ex shareholders. Solv-Ex declined to mention other possible parties involved.
In August, Solv-Ex filed suit against several short sellers.
Solv-Ex said recent press releases issued by Asensio & Co Inc, a short-seller of Solv-Ex, have attempted to discredit Solv-Ex and its progress in developing an oil plant.
Solv-Ex also said Manuel Asensio, a principal of Asensio & Co, has resisted its efforts to subpoena his records and take his deposition.
Asensio said Solv-Ex's allegations were without merit. He said he was within his rights to resist the subpoena and protect himself against an "invasion of privacy."
